2114053263477629420.author: nikstep
2114053263477629420.reply: If MCP access is a must, Notion is the easy pick: solid Mac and iPhone apps plus an official hosted MCP server, so Claude can read and write your notes. Obsidian also works through its Local REST API. Setup details: https://swarmnest.ai/directory/mcp-servers/notion-mcp/

2114354342866084308.author: NicStrel
2114354342866084308.reply: Those three are good first stops. The Official MCP Registry is the easiest: publish a server.json with the mcp-publisher CLI and verify your GitHub or domain namespace. Glama and awesome-mcp-servers are worth it too, and you can submit to Swarmnest here: https://swarmnest.ai/submit/

2114065925842604304.author: sanketvgh
2114065925842604304.reply: The ones that tend to stick: GitHub MCP for issues and PRs, Context7 for current library docs, Playwright for browser testing, and Sequential Thinking for planning. Keep it to two or three, since every extra server adds tool noise. More by use case: https://swarmnest.ai/directory/mcp-servers/

2114311121226416607.author: AlphaByPablo
2114311121226416607.reply: Try obra's systematic-debugging skill on a bug you've been stuck on. It makes the agent find the root cause before it touches any code, so it's easy to judge against Claude's default behavior. https://swarmnest.ai/agent-skills/obra-systematic-debugging/

2114611809269522941.author: akramcodez
2114611809269522941.reply: Start with obra's Superpowers set: writing-plans before big changes, test-driven-development, and verification-before-completion so it proves a fix works before saying done. Addy Osmani's code-simplification skill pairs well. https://swarmnest.ai/agent-skills/obra-using-superpowers/

2114542483095040281.author: nischal
2114542483095040281.reply: Closest building block is Have I Been Pwned's Pwned Passwords API. It uses k-anonymity, so an agent sends only a 5-character hash prefix and the password never leaves your machine. For reuse, your password manager's audit is the safer source. https://swarmnest.ai/directory/code-security/have-i-been-pwned-api/

2114580540045091038.author: farook_fazrin
2114580540045091038.reply: Microsoft's official one is the Microsoft Learn MCP server. It's free, needs no auth, and gives your agent current .NET and C# docs plus code samples. To build your own, the official MCP C# SDK is the way in. https://swarmnest.ai/directory/mcp-servers/microsoft-learn-mcp-server/

2115762408388255788.author: lcy362
2115762408388255788.reply: For full desktops, Cua is worth a look: it gives agents sandboxed macOS and Linux VMs plus a desktop driver, so they can drive any app, not just the browser. Keep CDP or Playwright for web work, since it is faster and more reliable there. https://swarmnest.ai/directory/mac-ai-agent-apps/cua/

2115814159824945562.author: bradvin
2115814159824945562.reply: One approach: make a single Claude Code or Codex session the lead, have it hand independent tasks to subagents, and only review what comes back. obra's dispatching-parallel-agents skill teaches that split, and when not to use it. https://swarmnest.ai/agent-skills/obra-dispatching-parallel-agents/

2115934441411674600.author: JesseFriedland
2115934441411674600.reply: Mealie gets close: it imports recipes from any URL, has a weekly meal planner and shared households, and works on your phone as a web app. Self-hosted, with a REST API and community MCP servers. Tandoor and RecipeSage are close too. https://swarmnest.ai/directory/recipes-cooking/

2115833251184902479.author: theKirillV
2115833251184902479.reply: You can wire them together: run claude mcp serve and add Claude Code as an MCP server in the Claude desktop app's config. The chat can then call Claude Code's file and command tools directly, so no more copy-paste. https://swarmnest.ai/directory/ai-coding-assistants/claude-code/

2115823665543852073.author: itsjoenaso
2115823665543852073.reply: It starts to feel different when tools match jobs instead of endpoints: one find_overdue_invoices call that chains three API requests and returns only what the model needs. A 1:1 API mirror leaves all that planning to the model. https://swarmnest.ai/guides/best-mcp-servers-for-claude-code-and-cursor/

2115878715477618829.author: chiranjeevkap
2115878715477618829.reply: Start with Anthropic's frontend-design skill: it pushes Claude past generic layouts toward bolder type, color and motion. Pair it with Vercel's web-design-guidelines for accessibility and UX checks. More in one place: https://swarmnest.ai/agent-skills/category/frontend-skills/

2116038045829054688.author: _pragmatic_dev
2116038045829054688.reply: The one most devs keep on daily is Context7: it gives the agent current library docs instead of stale training data. Then Playwright for checking UI in a real browser and GitHub MCP for issues and PRs. A few servers beat a long list. https://swarmnest.ai/directory/mcp-servers/context7/
